To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the six genes that control matrix production and fibroprolferation are expressed in the lung at higher levels in the anatomic regions of the lung where asbestos fibres deposit, and that the level of expression increases with time after exposure and with increasing fibre deposition.

the six genes that control matrix production and proliferation are expressed at significantly different levels depending on the number of asbestos fibres that deposit at the individual anatomical site and the length of the exposure.
the six genes are upregulated in a dose‐dependent manner in situ, in the lung, in response to asbestos inhalation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the early events of fibroprolificative lung disease
the identification of the genes that mediate the pathogenesis of fibroprolificative lung disease

identifying the genes that are involved in the fibroprolificative response to asbestos exposure, and this study provides the first evidence that these genes are expressed in a dose–response manner in situ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the six genes are expressed in situ in the lungs of the mice in a dose–response manner, and that this dose–response is dependent on the number and distribution of asbestos fibres that deposit at the individual anatomical site.
the genes are expressed at higher levels in the fibrotic regions, the fibrotic region is dose‐dependent, and the BAD junctions are the most fibrotic regions.
the six genes examined in this study are upregulated in a dose–response manner by asbestos fibres in the mouse lung.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the genes we examined are expressed at significantly greater levels in fibroproliterative lesions that develop in the lungs of asbestos‐exposed animals, and these lesions are dependent on the number and location of asbestos fibres that deposit.
asbestos‐induced fibrogenesis in the mouse lung is a dose‐dependent process, and the fibrogenic response is initiated at the BAD junction.
the six genes are expressed in the same anatomic sites that exhibit fibrosis, and that the level of expression is dependent on the number and location of the asbestos fibres.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dose–response of genes that control lung fibrosis is dependent on the anatomic region of the lung, and the number of fibroprolificative genes expressed in the BAD junctions is greater than in any other anatomic region.
the fibrotic process begins at the BAD junction, and this is the most sensitive site to asbestos exposure.
the genes coding the proteins that mediate fibrosis are expressed in fibrotic lesions in situ, and their expression is dose dependent.
